This comes as the company maintained one of the largest cash piles in the U.S. and posted revenue of $89.50 billion, exceeding Wall Street expectations despite analysts predicting a fourth consecutive quarter of revenue decline.

headline: Globalstar's new CEO keeps things vague – for now
content: Globalstar's new CEO, Paul Jacobs, addressed the company's future plans for the first time since taking the helm approximately two months ago. While optimistic about the combination of space and terrestrial assets, Jacobs provided few concrete details, stating he is still reviewing operations and initiatives, including previously announced private wireless network deals. He expressed hope for an agreement within a year for monetizing spectrum assets and highlighted Globalstar's role in direct-to-cell services and IoT, as the company reported increased revenue and raised full-year guidance.

headline: Understanding the Role of Chatbots in Virtual Care Delivery
content: Chatbots are increasingly vital in virtual healthcare delivery, offering applications from administrative tasks like scheduling appointments to clinical uses such as patient triage and mental health support. While they provide significant benefits in efficiency and patient satisfaction, concerns persist regarding their ability to handle complex diagnostic scenarios, data privacy, and HIPAA compliance, requiring ongoing efforts to build trust among both physicians and patients. The article details chatbot categories, their diverse use cases in virtual care, and weighs their benefits against current limitations.

headline: 'We're Changing the Structure:' GM's Software Boss Steps Down Amid Major Overhaul
content: General Motors is reorganizing its software and services engineering team, leading to the departure of former Apple executive Dave Richardson, who was VP of software and services engineering. Sterling Anderson, GM's chief product officer, will now oversee vehicle software engineering and Global Product. This change aims to accelerate the development and delivery of technology experiences as GM prepares to launch a new centralized computer system in 2028 and moves away from phone mirroring in future vehicles.

headline: Cyberattack Hits Infosys' McCamish Systems, Disrupting Operations
content: Infosys' step-down subsidiary, Infosys McCamish Systems, experienced a cyberattack that caused the non-availability of certain applications and systems. The company is collaborating with a cybersecurity products provider and has launched an independent investigation to determine the impact on systems and data. This incident adds to a growing concern about cybersecurity, following other significant breaches and warnings of state-sponsored attacks earlier this year.

headline: On-device AI chips: New battleground for chipmakers
content: Global chipmakers like Samsung Electronics, Qualcomm, Intel, and AMD are intensifying their focus on on-device AI chips for smartphones, laptops, and PCs, recognizing its potential for customized services, lower costs, and enhanced privacy compared to generative AI. This shift is expected to drive significant growth in AI-enabled consumer electronics and contribute to rising memory chip prices. Both on-device AI and generative AI are seen as complementary, with companies like Samsung planning to integrate both into future smart devices.
source: The Korea Economic Daily Global Edition

headline: Starbucks raising wages at least 3% starting Jan. 1
content: Starbucks announced it will raise wages for its U.S. retail hourly partners by at least 3% starting January 1, 2024, with more tenured employees receiving higher increases up to 5%. This move is part of an expanded benefits package and comes without anticipated menu price increases. The company stated these investments aim to improve the partner experience, reduce turnover, and enhance customer connection scores.

headline: Why Warren Buffett has done more to educate investors than any other corporate executive
content: Warren Buffett, CEO of Berkshire Hathaway and a prominent figure on the MarketWatch 50 list, is recognized for his significant influence on investors. He is known for his candid communication, explaining complex business operations, and openly discussing his successes and failures, which has made him an exceptional educator in the investment world.

headline: Apple agrees to $25 million settlement with US over hiring of immigrants
content: Apple Inc. has agreed to pay $25 million to settle claims by the U.S. Department of Justice that it illegally favored immigrant workers over U.S. citizens and green card holders for certain jobs. The Justice Department stated that Apple did not recruit U.S. citizens or permanent residents for jobs eligible for a federal program allowing employers to sponsor immigrant workers for green cards. This settlement marks the largest ever for the Justice Department concerning discrimination based on citizenship.

headline: Lionsgate Increases Majority Stake In 3 Arts Entertainment
content: Lionsgate Entertainment is finalizing a deal to acquire an additional, significant ownership stake in management and production company 3 Arts Entertainment. This move follows Lionsgate's initial majority stake acquisition in 2018 and comes after months of negotiations and a new valuation. The partnership has been fruitful, contributing five recent shows to Lionsgate’s TV series slate, including "Mythic Quest" and "The Serpent Queen."

headline: Booking.com settles Italian tax dispute with 94-million euro payment
content: Travel website Booking.com has agreed to pay approximately 94 million euros ($100.25 million) to settle a tax dispute in Italy covering the period from 2013 to 2021. The settlement follows an investigation by Genoa prosecutors into the company's handling of VAT on properties rented through its platform. As part of the agreement, Booking.com also filed its VAT return in Italy for 2022 and committed to acting as a tax substitute for transactions with private individuals not registered for VAT.

headline: Qualcomm and Iridium end their satellite chip partnership
content: Mobile chip giant Qualcomm has terminated its satellite-to-phone partnership with Iridium, less than a year after its announcement. The collaboration, which aimed to provide satellite-to-phone services via Snapdragon Satellite and Iridium's satellites, struggled due to a lack of adoption by smartphone manufacturers who preferred standards-based solutions. Both companies plan to continue exploring standards-based satellite connectivity options, with Iridium now free to engage directly with OEMs and chipmakers.

headline: Amazon sued over 'dangerous partnership' with virtual casino apps
content: Amazon is being sued in a proposed consumer class-action lawsuit for allegedly earning billions through an "illegal internet gambling enterprise." The lawsuit, filed by a Nevada resident, claims Amazon distributed over 30 illegal casino apps and processed payments for virtual chips, maintaining a 30% financial interest. This case is part of broader litigation targeting online social casino apps, with similar lawsuits pending against Apple, Meta, and Google regarding their payment-processing roles.

headline: FAANG Gives Way to the ‘Magnificent Seven’
content: The "FAANG" stock group has evolved into the "Magnificent Seven," with Netflix replaced by Nvidia, and Microsoft and Tesla added to the mix of top U.S. market names. ETF issuers are beginning to launch products specifically targeting these seven stocks, while existing ETFs like the Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF (MGK) already hold significant concentrations of them. Investors have various options, from highly concentrated ETFs to diversified funds, to gain exposure to these influential companies.

headline: Market Edges: The Recession (And Fourth Turning) Are Here
content: Hedgeye argues that a recession is currently underway, contrary to investor hopes for a "Santa Claus rally" and standard seasonal trends. They emphasize a data-driven approach ("conditional factoring") over seasonal optimism, providing extensive resources and analysis of dire economic indicators like household debt, credit delinquencies, and retail sector weakness. The article also highlights insights from Demography analyst Neil Howe on "The Fourth Turning" and global recessionary signals from currency and commodity markets.

headline: QYLD ETF Analysis: Dividends, Returns NASDAQ:QYLD
content: This article provides an analysis of the Global X NASDAQ 100 Covered Call ETF (QYLD), focusing on its dividends and returns. It highlights QYLD's strategy of generating income by selling covered call options on the Nasdaq-100, resulting in a less volatile return pattern compared to traditional Nasdaq-100 ETFs. The analysis covers key statistics such as AUM, dividend yield, expense ratio, holdings, and historical performance, alongside frequently asked questions about the fund.

headline: Spotlight on XYLD: An S&P 500 Covered Call Strategy
content: This article highlights the Global X S&P 500 Covered Call ETF (XYLD) as a strategy for investors looking to reduce volatility and generate income in the current market environment. It explains how XYLD uses a buy/write strategy by selling call options on the S&P 500 Index to produce a competitive yield, which exceeded 11% as of September 2023. The article also suggests that XYLD may be particularly appealing in a sideways-moving market, providing diversification and income for defensive investors.

headline: FMR LLC Acquires New Stake in Magenta Therapeutics Inc
content: FMR LLC, through its flagship company Fidelity Investments, has acquired a new stake in Magenta Therapeutics Inc (MGTA) by purchasing 2,218,212 shares at $0.6996 per share. This transaction gives FMR LLC a 14.97% ownership stake in the clinical-stage biotechnology company, indicating a strategic investment aligning with the firm's focus on technology and healthcare sectors. Despite Magenta Therapeutics currently operating at a loss, FMR LLC's move suggests a belief in the company's long-term value and transformative potential in stem cell and gene therapy.

headline: FMR LLC Bolsters Portfolio with Fidelity International Value Fac
content: FMR LLC, also known as Fidelity, has significantly expanded its investment portfolio by acquiring 350,126 shares of the Fidelity International Value Factor ETF (FIVA) at $21.95 per share. This transaction, executed on October 31, 2023, increases FMR LLC's holdings in FIVA to 1,099,261 shares, representing a 32.33% position in its portfolio. The move reflects Fidelity's strategic investment in an ETF that has shown a 9.1% year-to-date performance.

headline: Spotlight on illegal hiring practices: Apple pays $25M for recruiting, job ad mistakes
content: Apple Inc. has agreed to pay $25 million to settle allegations of illegal hiring practices related to its PERM program. A DOJ investigation found Apple failed to recruit U.S. citizens or green card holders, did not advertise these positions on its external website, and required paper applications for PERM jobs while allowing electronic applications for others. The settlement includes $18.25 million for discrimination victims and $6.75 million for civil penalties, with Apple also agreeing to revise its recruitment practices and provide employee training.

headline: Tepper’s Appaloosa dumps Apple stake and loads up on Amazon’s stock
content: David Tepper’s Appaloosa hedge fund significantly increased its stake in Amazon.com Inc. and completely divested its position in Apple Inc. during the last quarter. The fund also raised its holdings in Google parent Alphabet Inc. and Facebook parent Meta Platforms Inc., as detailed in a recent SEC filing. This move indicates a shift in Tepper's portfolio allocation towards these tech giants.

headline: What's next for satellite communications on Android?
content: Apple has extended its Emergency SOS via satellite service for iPhone 14 and 15 users to two years, while Qualcomm's Snapdragon Satellite initiative for Android has failed due to lack of OEM integration. This leaves Iridium, a key satellite provider, free to pursue new partnerships directly with smartphone makers. The future of satellite communication on Android is unclear, though Samsung is rumored to introduce a solution with the Galaxy S24, and current options include standalone devices like the Motorola Defy Sat Link and Garmin inReach Mini 2.

headline: Unity 6 debuts next year with AI-powered innovations and platform updates
content: Unity announced its upcoming Unity 6 platform, set to launch in 2024, featuring significant AI innovations and platform updates. Key announcements from the Unite conference include the early access of Unity Muse for content creation, a preview of Unity 6, and the introduction of Unity Cloud. These updates aim to address developer feedback and enhance the game development process following recent controversies over pricing changes.

headline: Warren Buffet's latest buys and sells
content: This article details Berkshire Hathaway's latest stock buys and sells from its third-quarter 2023 13F filing, highlighting that the company was a net seller despite a tough market quarter, leading to a record cash stake. It identifies three undervalued Warren Buffett stocks within Berkshire Hathaway’s portfolio—Bank of America, American Express, and Kraft Heinz—providing Morningstar's analysis and key metrics for each. The piece also lists the stocks Berkshire Hathaway sold entirely, including Activision Blizzard, Celanese, General Motors, Johnson & Johnson, Mondelez International, Procter & Gamble, and United Parcel Service, while noting a significant reduction in its Chevron holdings.

headline: AT&T’s Black Friday Deals on the iPhone 15 Pro & More
content: AT&T announced its Black Friday deals for the holiday season, offering significant savings on various Apple products including the iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15, iPhone 14, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone SE 3rd Gen, iPad, and Apple Watch. Deals include trade-in options, no trade-in required offers, and low monthly payments, catering to both new and existing customers. Additionally, AT&T highlighted benefits like flexible shopping, unlimited plans with 5G access, AT&T Fiber deals, and special discounts for military, veterans, teachers, nurses, and physicians.

headline: Warren Buffett Has Bought Shares of This Stock for 21 Consecutive Quarters -- and It's Not Apple
content: Warren Buffett has consistently invested in Berkshire Hathaway's own stock for 21 consecutive quarters, authorizing over $72 billion in repurchases since mid-2018. This strategy, enabled by a change in buyback clauses, aims to reward long-term shareholders by increasing their ownership stakes and potentially boosting earnings per share. While Apple constitutes nearly half of Berkshire's invested assets, the frequent repurchase of Berkshire Hathaway shares itself highlights Buffett's conviction in his own company.

headline: Network of Lies review: Brian Stelter on Fox News, Trump and Dominion
content: Brian Stelter's book "Network of Lies" examines Fox News's role in spreading election conspiracies following the 2020 election, leading to significant legal and financial repercussions, such as the Dominion settlement. The review highlights Rupert Murdoch's recent step down, the Murdochs' balancing act of profitability and audience satisfaction, and the ongoing influence of Donald Trump on the network and Republican politics. Despite the controversies, the article suggests little change is expected from Fox News as it navigates complex defamation lawsuits and competitive political landscapes.

headline: Apple’s In-House Technologies Team Still Has Plenty of Work to Do
content: This article discusses Apple's intensive efforts to design and manufacture its own core hardware components, such as cameras, screens, modems, and batteries, for its products. It also touches on Apple's adoption of the RCS texting standard, the revelation of its revenue share from the Google search deal, and a key health executive's move to Oura. The piece highlights that Apple's in-house technologies team has extensive work ahead in its strategic initiative to control major parts of its devices.

headline: Should You Buy the Invesco QQQ ETF With the Nasdaq At An All-Time High? History Offers a Clear Answer.
content: This article discusses the Invesco QQQ ETF and whether it's a good investment despite the Nasdaq Composite being at an all-time high. It analyzes historical data of the Nasdaq's performance after reaching new highs, suggesting that further gains are common. The article concludes that dollar-cost averaging into QQQ is a sensible strategy regardless of market highs, as it tracks the Nasdaq 100 which tends to rise over time.

headline: Venmo, Cash App users sue Apple over peer-to-peer payment fees
content: Venmo and Cash App customers have filed a proposed class-action lawsuit against Apple Inc. alleging the company abused its market power in mobile peer-to-peer payments, leading to "rapidly inflating prices." The lawsuit claims Apple's agreements with PayPal's Venmo and Block's Cash App violate U.S. antitrust law by limiting "feature competition," including prohibiting decentralized cryptocurrency technology. This case adds to Apple's ongoing antitrust legal challenges, seeking an injunction that could force Apple to divest or segregate its Apple Cash business.

headline: Gaming Industry Charts a Rebound in 2023
content: The gaming industry is experiencing a significant rebound in 2023 driven by strong console sales, new game releases, and innovations in mobile and cloud gaming. This recovery, following a dip in 2022, is further supported by anticipation of increased M&A activity and strategic moves by major players like Microsoft, Apple, and Netflix, positioning the sector for continued growth into 2024. The article highlights strong U.S. sales, hardware as a primary catalyst, and key factors like M&A and technological advancements shaping the industry's future trajectory.

headline: InterDigital’s Alain Mourad Elected Chair of New ETSI Industry Specification Group on Integrated Sensing and Communications
content: Dr. Alain Mourad, Head of InterDigital’s Wireless Lab Europe, has been elected Chair of the newly formed ETSI Industry Specification Group (ISG) on Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC). This group aims to establish the technical foundation for ISAC technology and its standardization in 6G, defining use cases and developing evaluation roadmaps. The ISG will also study privacy, security, and sustainability aspects of ISAC within the 6G framework.

headline: Sonos Readies $400-Plus Headphones to Rival Apple and Bose, TV Set-Top Box
content: Sonos Inc. is planning a significant expansion into new product categories, including headphones priced over $400 and a TV set-top box. These new offerings are expected to compete with products from Apple, Bose, and Roku, marking a strategic move beyond its traditional smart speakers and sound bars. The headphones could launch as early as April, with the set-top box following by the end of 2024.

headline: Department of Justice and Apple Reach $25 Million Landmark Agreement
content: The U.S. Department of Justice announced a $25 million agreement with Apple Inc. to resolve allegations of discriminatory hiring practices related to the permanent labor certification (PERM) program. Apple's recruitment practices for PERM positions, which included not advertising on its public-facing career website and requiring mailed paper applications, deterred U.S. workers. The settlement includes $6.75 million in civil penalties and $18.25 million for a backpay fund for victims, and mandates Apple to align PERM recruitment with its standard practices.

headline: OpenAI Says Sam Altman to Return as CEO in Dramatic Reversal
content: Sam Altman is set to return as CEO of OpenAI after being ousted less than a week prior, following intense negotiations and pressure from investors like Microsoft and nearly all of the company's employees. The agreement includes a new initial board of directors led by Bret Taylor, with Larry Summers and Adam D’Angelo, and an internal investigation into the conduct that led to Altman's dismissal. This dramatic reversal comes after widespread calls for Altman's reinstatement and highlights the significant influence of investors and employees on the future of the AI startup.

headline: Sonos is reportedly working on a streaming video TV set top box, along with headphones
content: Sonos is reportedly expanding its product line beyond speakers and soundbars. The company isSaid to be working on over-the-ear headphones for a March 2024 launch, possibly priced between $400 and $500, and high-end earbuds. Additionally, Sonos is reportedly developing an Android-based streaming video TV set-top box, codenamed "Pinewood," which could launch in late 2024 or early 2025.

headline: Warren Buffett-Led Berkshire Hathaway Sells Its Entire Procter & Gamble Stake. Should You?
content: Berkshire Hathaway fully exited its small position in Procter & Gamble, likely due to consolidating its portfolio and P&G's premium valuation compared to other opportunities like Apple. Despite Berkshire's sale, P&G is still considered a worthwhile investment for risk-averse individuals due to its strong brand development, pricing power, and commitment to shareholder returns through dividends and buybacks. The article suggests that while P&G's valuation is high, its other characteristics make it a solid choice for passive income and portfolio stability.

headline: Deere must face US farmers' 'right-to-repair' lawsuits, judge rules
content: A U.S. judge has ruled that Deere & Co must face consolidated lawsuits from farmers accusing the agricultural machinery maker of unlawfully conspiring to restrict maintenance and repair services. The judge rejected Deere's arguments for dismissal, stating that the plaintiffs met the legal thresholds to pursue their antitrust claims. This case is part of a broader "right-to-repair" movement challenging restrictive repair practices across various industries.

headline: $2 billion semiconductor testing and packaging facility planned for Peoria
content: Amkor Technology Inc. plans to build a $2 billion semiconductor testing and advanced packaging facility in Peoria, Arizona, near the TSMC plant. This facility, expected to create 2,000 jobs, will test and package chips for Apple and aims to strengthen the domestic semiconductor supply chain. The project is seen as a crucial step for Arizona's semiconductor ecosystem and national security.

headline: AI ETFs see huge performance dispersion in 2023
content: Artificial Intelligence ETFs have shown significant performance dispersion in 2023, with top strategies more than doubling the returns of the lowest performers. This disparity is largely attributed to the heavy weighting of certain ETFs towards US equities and the "magnificent seven" tech stocks. While these mega-cap companies have driven much of the AI theme's returns, there is still potential for pure-play AI companies to join the rally.

headline: Amkor Announces U.S. Advanced Packaging and Test Facility In Peoria
content: Amkor Technology, Inc. announced a $2 billion investment to build an advanced packaging and test facility in Peoria, Arizona, creating 2,000 new jobs. This facility will be the largest outsourced advanced packaging facility in the US, bolstering America's national security and semiconductor supply chain. Apple will be the first and largest customer, and Amkor has applied for CHIPS funding to support the project.

headline: Amkor to build $2 billion semiconductor testing plant in Peoria. 2,000 jobs promised
content: Amkor Technology Inc. plans to build a $2 billion advanced semiconductor packaging and testing facility in Peoria, Arizona, creating approximately 2,000 jobs. The plant will partner with TSMC, testing chips produced for Apple Inc., and is expected to begin production within two to three years. This investment is seen as a significant step in bolstering the U.S. semiconductor supply chain and is supported by the CHIPS and Science Act.

headline: Apple Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
content: Apple Inc. (AAPL) stock rose by 0.31% to $189.95 on Thursday, outperforming the mixed stock market session which saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average rise and the NASDAQ Composite Index fall. The company's shares closed $8.28 below their 52-week high.

headline: Apple announces expanded partnership with Amkor for advanced silicon packaging in the U.S.
content: Apple announced an expanded partnership with Amkor, designating Apple as the first and largest customer for Amkor's new manufacturing and packaging facility in Peoria, Arizona. This facility will package Apple silicon produced at the nearby TSMC fab, strengthening Apple's commitment to American manufacturing. Amkor plans to invest approximately $2 billion in the project, creating over 2,000 jobs, as part of Apple's broader commitment to invest $430 billion in the U.S. economy.

headline: Apple to become largest customer of new $2B chip packaging facility in Arizona
content: Apple announced it will be the primary customer for Amkor Technology Inc.'s new $2 billion chip packaging facility in Arizona, which will package chips produced by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) at a nearby complex. This facility will play a crucial role in assembling and protecting the next generation of processors for various Apple products. The investment underscores Apple's commitment to American manufacturing and will create over 2,000 jobs.

headline: Cognizant Technology Solutions to lay off employees tied to Apple in Austin
content: Cognizant Technology Solutions announced layoffs impacting employees linked to Apple in Austin. The contractors affected will receive pay while exploring other positions within Cognizant. This move adds to a series of technology sector layoffs in Austin, though Central Texas is noted to be somewhat sheltered from broader industry cuts.

headline: Who says corporate bonds are dull? Apple’s bonds have seen equity-like returns in the past month
content: Apple Inc. bonds have generated equity-like returns for investors in the past month, with prices climbing as Treasury yields have tumbled. This rally, fueled by hopes for Federal Reserve rate cuts in 2024, has led to significant gains in the broader fixed-income market, with the Bloomberg US Aggregate Bond Index seeing its biggest monthly gain since May 1985.

headline: One ETF that focuses on employee happiness is outperforming the market this year
content: An ETF focused on companies with high employee happiness, the Harbor Human Capital Factor U.S. Large Cap ETF (HAPI), has outperformed the S&P 500 this year, climbing nearly 25% compared to the benchmark's less than 20% gain. The fund's strategy is based on Irrational Capital's extensive employee surveys and publicly available data, creating a "human capital score" that is considered a novel and uncorrelated investment factor. While the large-cap HAPI fund includes major tech stocks contributing to its performance, a similar small-cap ETF (HAPS) is also available, offering potential for future growth.

headline: Walmart stops advertising on X, adding to growing list of companies
content: Walmart has ceased advertising on X, joining several other major companies like Apple, Disney, and IBM, citing that it found other platforms to better reach its customers. This decision was part of a gradual reduction in advertising on X, not a sudden halt, according to a source familiar with the situation and an X executive. The social media platform has faced a significant exodus of advertisers due to concerns over antisemitic content, exacerbated by recent controversies involving Elon Musk's comments and his subsequent strong reaction to advertisers.

headline: Amkor to invest US$2bn in US chip packaging
content: Amkor Technology Inc. plans to invest US$2 billion to build an advanced semiconductor packaging facility in Peoria, Arizona. This new plant will create up to 2,000 jobs and is expected to start production within two to three years, primarily packaging chips made for Apple by TSMC in Phoenix. The investment aims to bolster the US’s chipmaking capabilities, reduce reliance on foreign packaging capacity, and has applied for Chips Act funding.

headline: Sonos roadmap reveals multiple audio launches intended in 2024
content: Sonos is planning an "aggressive" roadmap of new audio products and software updates for 2024, including new in-ceiling speakers, headphones, a second-generation Roam, a high-end amplifier, and a high-end soundbar. A set-top box and subwoofer are also planned for late 2024 or 2025 releases. The company aims to revive sales through these launches, despite facing skepticism in competitive markets.

headline: This Growth-Focused ETF Makes for an Excellent Long-Term Investment
content: The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is highlighted as an excellent long-term investment, having seen a 46% gain this year due to its focus on growth stocks. QQQ tracks the NASDAQ-100 Index, which includes 100 of the largest non-financial companies on the NASDAQ, with a heavy concentration in technology giants like Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft. The ETF offers investors diversified exposure within the tech sector and has historically shown strong performance, more than doubling in value over five years, making it suitable for maximizing returns.

headline: 美股科技股“疯牛”行情未完待续? AI仍是引爆明年行情的关键
content: Wedbush機構預計美股科技股在2024年將上漲至少20%，主要得益於人工智能（AI）和雲計算支出的大幅增長。分析師將AI比作互聯網的“1995時刻”，預計未來十年AI支出規模將達到1萬億美元，並點名英偉達和微軟將引領這一趨勢。儘管宏觀經濟不確定性存在，Wedbush仍堅定看好科技行業，並預計納斯達克100指數明年在高科技巨頭帶領下將大漲20%以上。

headline: Amex CEO talks co-brand partnerships after Apple reports
content: American Express CEO Steve Squeri discussed co-branded partnerships, emphasizing that Amex's "premium" card designation means it doesn't align with all potential partners, a point highlighted amidst reports of Amex potentially replacing Goldman Sachs as Apple's credit card partner. Squeri noted that Amex seeks partnerships that offer strong value propositions, target premium customers, and provide distribution while yielding "premium economics." Analysts have speculated on several potential suitors for Apple's card partnership, including Amex, JPMorgan Chase, Synchrony Financial, Capital One, and Bread.

headline: Why Investors Should Keep An Eye on Small-Cap Stocks
content: This article discusses how the increasing concentration of market-cap-weighted indexes, particularly driven by large-cap tech stocks, is creating historical levels of concentration. It explores the implications for the size premium, suggesting that higher market concentration leads to increased expected returns for small-cap stocks due to capital misallocation and reduced investor demand for smaller firms, making them an attractive area for investors.

headline: CastleArk Enters ETF Market With Large Growth ETF CARK
content: CastleArk has launched its first exchange-traded fund, the CastleArk Large Growth ETF (CARK), an actively managed ETF focused on large-cap growth companies. The fund targets 25-30 leading growth companies, identifying competitive strength and seeking to optimize risk through quantitative inputs. CastleArk aims to provide an actively managed alternative to index-heavy portfolios, especially given the concentration of "Magnificent Seven" stocks in the large-cap growth sector.

headline: TIDAL cuts 10% of staff as parent company Block enforces cost-saving measures
content: Music streaming service TIDAL has laid off 10% of its workforce, impacting about 40 employees, as part of parent company Block Inc.'s cost-saving measures. This move aligns with Block CEO Jack Dorsey's November letter to investors, stating the company's intent to cap payroll at 12,000 employees. The layoffs at TIDAL reflect a broader trend of staff reductions across the tech and music industries, following similar cuts by companies like Spotify, Amazon, Google, and Meta.

headline: Tesla’s Dojo Supercomputer Head Exits in Blow to Efforts
content: Ganesh Venkataramanan, the head of Tesla's Dojo supercomputer project, has left the company after five years, posing a significant setback to the automaker's self-driving technology endeavors. Peter Bannon, a long-time Tesla director and former Apple executive, has taken over leadership of the project. This departure comes as Tesla plans to invest over $1 billion in Dojo by the end of 2024, a project analysts believe could add $500 billion to Tesla's valuation.

headline: Who’s ready for a Gamestop mutual fund? Not this broker
content: Wedbush analysts are critical of GameStop's decision to delegate investment authority to CEO Ryan Cohen, allowing him to invest the company's capital in equities and other investments. Analyst Michael Pachter suggests that if GameStop believes in its own shares, it should use excess cash for buybacks instead. The move is compared to AMC's "embarrassingly stupid" investment in Hycroft Mining, which saw significant losses.

headline: Just 3 of the "Magnificent Seven" Have Outperformed the S&P 500 Since 2022. Here's the One I'd Buy for 2024 and 2025.
content: This article analyzes the performance of the "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks against the S&P 500 since 2022. It identifies Nvidia, Microsoft, and Apple as the only three that have outperformed the S&P 500. The author argues that Alphabet, despite underperforming recently, is the best buy for 2024 and 2025 due to its valuation, potential in digital advertising, and cloud segment growth.

headline: 'You have to be difficult': How Gap and J.Crew icon Mickey Drexler became the king of mall-brand retail
content: This article details how Mickey Drexler, a prominent figure in retail, transformed Gap and revitalized J.Crew, known for his unconventional leadership. He also founded Old Navy and Madewell, served on Apple's board, and heavily influenced Alex Mill, a company started by his son. Drexler is characterized by his micromanagement style and significant impact on several successful brands.

headline: Themes Generative Artificial Intelligence ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:WISE)
content: The Themes Generative Artificial Intelligence ETF (WISE) tracks an index of companies involved in AI-related industries, with a concentrated portfolio of 89 holdings. Launched on December 8, 2023, the ETF currently has $33.55 million in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.35%. Its top holdings include major tech companies like Advanced Micro Devices, Intel, Apple, and NVIDIA.

headline: The Nasdaq-100 Has Had a Monster 2023 So Far. Is It Too Late to Invest in It Before 2024 Arrives?
content: The Nasdaq-100 has seen a significant rally of 45% in 2023 after a difficult 2022, outperforming other major U.S. indexes. Despite this strong performance, the article suggests that it's not too late to invest, emphasizing a long-term approach and dollar-cost averaging to mitigate short-term volatility. It highlights the Invesco QQQ ETF as a common way to invest in the Nasdaq-100, composed of innovative companies poised for continued growth in industries like AI, EVs, and biotech.

headline: Apple supplier Corning to set up Rs 1,000 crore Gorilla Glass facility in Tamil Nadu
content: Corning Inc., a key Apple supplier and Gorilla Glass manufacturer, plans to invest Rs 1,000 crore in a new manufacturing plant in Tamil Nadu, India. This facility, a collaboration with Indian partner Optiemus Infracom, will be located near other Apple suppliers and is expected to start operations in 2024, initially producing 30 million pieces of cover glass for smartphones. The move comes after Corning chose Tamil Nadu over Telangana, seeking central government incentives under the SPECS scheme.

headline: Buffett's Berkshire Slashes Losing HP Bet by Nearly 60% in 3 Months
content: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has significantly reduced its stake in HP by 57% since mid-September, selling off nearly 60% of its holdings and cutting its ownership from over 12% to about 5%. This move comes as HP has been a losing bet for Berkshire, with the firm selling shares below its initial purchase price from early 2022. Berkshire has been actively paring back its stock portfolio recently, accumulating a record cash pile.

headline: How Google’s Epic Legal Defeat Threatens the App-Store Industry’s $200 Billion Business Model
content: Google's recent legal defeat against Epic Games threatens the $200 billion app store industry, which includes Apple. A jury found Google's app store practices anticompetitive, which could lead to significant changes in commission rates and developer options. This verdict could also impact Apple's similar business model, despite its previous victory against Epic, as regulators and lawmakers globally scrutinize app store rules and consumer sentiment leans against the power of tech giants.

headline: DGRW Has Hallmarks of a Great Dividend ETF
content: The WisdomTree US Quality Dividend Growth Fund (DGRW) is highlighted as a strong dividend ETF due to its focus on companies' return on assets and return on equity, rather than just yield. This strategy has allowed DGRW to outperform the S&P 500 and other dividend indexes, especially in high-interest-rate environments. The ETF's approach aims for reduced volatility, potential capital appreciation, and diversification, including a significant allocation to tech stocks.

headline: The Apple Inc (AAPL) DCF Valuation: Is The Stock Undervalued?
content: This article presents a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) valuation for Apple Inc. (AAPL) to determine if the stock is undervalued. Based on the DCF analysis, Apple's stock appears overvalued with a DCF value of $118.68 per share compared to a current market price of $198.08, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -66.91%. The author emphasizes that this is a preliminary analysis and investors should conduct further research.

headline: US Chamber, Comcast, tech group split over net neutrality
content: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce and Comcast Corp are opposing the Federal Communications Commission's proposal to reinstate net neutrality rules, arguing it would harm investment and innovation. Conversely, major tech firms like Amazon, Apple, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms support the reinstatement to preserve open internet access. The FCC's move to regain regulatory oversight, following Democrats taking majority control, aims to ensure a "fast, open, and fair" internet, while some states also have existing net neutrality laws.

headline: Call translation services new battleground in AI race
content: The coming year will see a surge in real-time phone call translation services driven by AI, with Korean tech firms like SK Telecom and Samsung Electronics entering the fray. SK Telecom is launching its "A. call translator" service within its existing AI app, supporting four languages initially and expanding to 11. Samsung, conversely, plans to integrate its generative AI model "Samsung Gauss" directly into its new Galaxy S24 phones, offering on-device translation without external internet access, emphasizing privacy and reduced latency.

headline: Focus: Exxon's low US tax payments ruffle Biden's climate agenda
content: Exxon Mobil's income tax payments to the U.S. government have significantly decreased to 3% over the past five years, mainly due to deductions passed under former President Donald Trump, frustrating the Biden administration's climate agenda. This low tax rate, much lower than major companies in other sectors, highlights how current tax codes impede efforts to fund green energy initiatives. Experts suggest Exxon could maintain these low tax rates for several more years, even as the government seeks more revenue for climate action, partly because President Biden's new minimum corporate tax struggles with implementation and still accounts for the Trump-era accelerated depreciation deductions.

headline: Apple Races to Tweak Software Ahead of Looming US Watch Ban
content: Apple Inc. is rapidly working on software adjustments to its Apple Watch series to circumvent a looming U.S. ban. The changes primarily target the blood oxygen level measurement feature, which a company called Masimo Corp. claims infringes on its patents. These modifications include altering algorithms for oxygen saturation detection and data presentation to consumers.

headline: Apple terminates credit-card and savings partnership with Goldman Sachs
content: Apple Inc. has initiated the termination of its credit card and savings account partnership with Goldman Sachs Group Inc., proposing to end the collaboration within 12 to 15 months. This move follows Goldman Sachs' struggles with its consumer banking division, which has incurred losses despite the strong performance of Apple Card and Apple Savings. Apple is now seeking a new banking provider, with JPMorgan Chase & Co. and American Express Company emerging as top contenders.

headline: Qorvo to sell Chinese assembly, test factories to Luxshare ...
content: Qorvo Inc. has agreed to sell its assembly and test facilities in Beijing and Dezhou, China, to Luxshare Precision Industry Co. Ltd. The deal includes Luxshare acquiring the facilities' assets, operations, and workforce, while Qorvo will continue to be supplied through a long-term agreement. This move allows Qorvo to streamline its manufacturing network while Luxshare expands its role in the electronics manufacturing services sector, particularly within the Apple supply chain.

headline: Why Apple Had to Disable the Blood-Oxygen Sensor in Its Watches
content: Apple has begun selling new versions of its latest Apple Watch models with the blood oxygen sensing feature disabled. This action stems from a patent dispute with Masimo Corp., a medical technology company, which successfully argued that Apple violated its patents. A US International Trade Commission ruling and subsequent appeals court decision led Apple to remove the feature rather than face a sales ban on its Watch Series 9 and Ultra 2 models.

headline: Meta: Sell it? Buy it?
content: Meta's stock price has experienced significant volatility in recent years, oscillating from a high of $384 in August 2021 to below $100 in October 2022, before rebounding to around $340. This article explores the company's journey from being considered a "sell" to a "buy," focusing on challenges such as Apple's privacy policy changes and competition from TikTok, and how Meta has responded by investing heavily in AI and re-evaluating its metaverse strategy. The future success of Meta is tied to its AI applications across its businesses, especially in advertising and new ventures.

headline: U.S. Fitness Tracker Market Size, Growth and Trends [2030]
content: The U.S. fitness tracker market was valued at USD 13.69 billion in 2022 and is projected to reach a significant size by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 18.9% during the forecast period. This growth is driven by the increasing prevalence of chronic diseases, high adoption of fitness monitoring devices, and technological advancements like integration with smartphones and advanced features. Despite potential inaccuracies, the market sees strong demand, particularly for smartwatches, with key players continuously innovating to meet consumer needs.

headline: Why These 3 Semiconductor Stocks Should Be on Your Radar in 2024
content: The article highlights three semiconductor stocks—Qualcomm (QCOM), United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC), and Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS)—that are poised for growth in 2024, driven by advancements in AI, electric vehicles, and 5G technology. It evaluates each company's market position, financial health, and growth catalysts, emphasizing their undervaluation and innovative contributions to the industry. The piece suggests these stocks offer high risk-reward opportunities for investors looking to capitalize on the expanding semiconductor market.

headline: Intellexa and Cytrox: From fixer-upper to Intel Agency-grade spyware
content: Cisco Talos has conducted an in-depth analysis of Intellexa, a spyware vendor previously known as Cytrox, detailing its operational paradigms, procedures, and the evolution of its Predator spyware. The analysis reveals that Intellexa's Predator spyware continues to evade detection, offers persistence even after device reboots, and demonstrates a sophisticated business model with high-priced solutions targeting state-sponsored agencies. Despite public disclosures and the US adding Intellexa to its Entity List, the company effectively continues its operations by adapting to patched exploits and maintaining plausible deniability through its sales and delivery methods.

headline: QARP ETF Analysis: Dividends, Returns AMEX:QARP
content: This article provides an analysis of the Xtrackers Russell 1000 US Quality at a Reasonable Price ETF (QARP), detailing its investment strategy, holdings, and performance. QARP focuses on US large-cap companies with a blend of quality and value metrics, giving twice as much weight to quality. The ETF has an expense ratio of 0.19% and aims to provide exposure to the Russell 1000 Slowdown Factor Index.

headline: PLDT warns public on AI-generated scams
content: PLDT and Smart Communications are warning the public about the rise of AI-generated scams, which are becoming increasingly sophisticated and convincing. Criminals are leveraging AI to create polished messages and visuals that mimic official communications, making it harder for individuals to distinguish genuine messages from fraudulent ones. PLDT advises checking the source of emails and texts and adhering to the basic rule of not communicating with strangers to avoid falling victim to these scams.

headline: Apple files appeal after Biden administration allows US ban on watch imports
content: Apple has appealed a U.S. import ban on its watches, which stems from a patent dispute with medical monitoring company Masimo. The ban, allowed by the Biden administration, targets Apple Watches with blood-oxygen level features. Apple has also requested an emergency halt to the ban while awaiting a decision from U.S. Customs and Border Protection on redesigned versions of its watches.

headline: How I used the Garmin epix Pro to train for Spartan Race's Trifecta Weekend
content: The author details their experience using the Garmin epix Pro to train for and complete Spartan Race's Trifecta Weekend, which involves finishing three races (Sprint, Super, Beast) in one weekend. The article highlights how the smartwatch's features like training readiness, body battery, heart rate monitoring, and race prediction were crucial for their rigorous training regimen and successful completion of the demanding events. The author expresses that the Garmin epix Pro not only enhanced their athletic performance but also motivated them toward healthier habits and served as a worthy investment in their fitness journey.

headline: T. Rowe Price Capital Appreciation Equity ETF (TCAF): A Promising Active Fund
content: The T. Rowe Price Capital Appreciation Equity ETF (TCAF) has shown significant growth since its launch in June 2023, accumulating over $600 million in assets. The fund focuses on high-quality U.S. large-cap companies, employing a bottom-up stock selection approach with top holdings like Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon. TCAF's investment philosophy emphasizes strong performance in areas like technology, healthcare, and consumer discretionary.

headline: Apple's stock underperformed top tech peers in 2023 due to longest revenue slide in 22 years
content: Apple's stock underperformed its mega-cap tech peers in 2023, experiencing its longest revenue slide in 22 years with four consecutive quarters of declining sales. This decline was attributed to a combination of a weak economic environment for smartphones and PCs, and company-specific issues such as the lack of new iPad models and an Apple Watch sales ban. Despite a 49% stock rally for the year, Apple lagged behind competitors like Nvidia, Meta, Tesla, Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft.

headline: Here Are All 49 Stocks Warren Buffett Holds for Berkshire Hathaway's $371 Billion Portfolio
content: This article details the 49 stocks held in Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway portfolio, valued at $371 billion. It highlights that over 85% of the assets are concentrated in eight major holdings like Apple and Bank of America, while also listing other billion-dollar investments and smaller holdings attributed to Buffett's lieutenants. The piece emphasizes Buffett's preference for financial and cyclical businesses, his valuation-driven approach, and recent investments in homebuilders.

headline: What to expect from Sonos in 2024 – headphones, new Arc and a big surprise
content: In 2024, Sonos is set to expand its product line significantly, venturing into new categories like premium over-ear headphones and potentially a streaming video box. The company also plans major upgrades to its existing portfolio, including an advanced voice control system (Voice 2.0), a second-generation Roam, and a new flagship Sonos Arc soundbar. These moves follow a challenging financial year for Sonos, indicating a strategy focused on growth and diversification.

headline: Cyber Hornet S&P 500 and Bitcoin 75/25 Strategy ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:ZZZ)
content: The Cyber Hornet S&P 500 and Bitcoin 75/25 Strategy ETF (ZZZ) is an exchange-traded fund launched on December 28, 2023, by Onefund, which invests in a 75/25 blend of US large-cap stocks and front-month CME Bitcoin futures. It does not directly invest in Bitcoin's spot price. The ETF has an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy," assets under management of $6.02 million, and a net expense ratio of 1.01%.

headline: Miami doesn’t need to be the Silicon Valley of the South
content: Miami has been hyped as a "new Silicon Valley" or "Silicon Valley of the South," but this article argues it should be recognized for its unique strengths rather than compared to Silicon Valley. The author highlights Miami's advantages, including favorable tax laws, a supportive tech ecosystem, increasing VC attention, strong foreign investment, a focus on AI, and its role as a bridge to Latin America for nearshoring. Miami's distinct features allow it to stand as its own specialized tech hub.

headline: Google and Samsung Set To Use Qualcomm's New VR Chip, Could Compete With Apple and Meta
content: Qualcomm (QCOM) recently unveiled its new Snapdragon XR2+ Gen 2 Platform chip for virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR). Google (GOOGL) and Samsung are slated to integrate this chip into their upcoming VR/AR experiences, aiming to challenge market leaders like Apple (AAPL) and Meta Platforms (META). This development could intensify competition in the growing VR headset market, especially following Apple's Vision Pro and Meta's dominance in 2023.

headline: Markets in Focus: Concentrating on Diversification
content: The article discusses the increasing concentration in equity markets, exemplified by the "Magnificent Seven" stocks, and the diminished diversification benefits of bonds, especially since 2020. It suggests that investors reassess top-down allocations and broaden equity exposure across diverse regions, sectors, and styles to create more resilient portfolios. The MSCI Adaptive Multi-Factor Allocation Model indicates an overweight to value and low size as of December 31, 2023, with Europe and China trading at lower historical valuations.

headline: Mindlessly scroll on bike? ‘Tiktok fitness powered by Peloton’, stock soars
content: Peloton has announced a partnership with TikTok to create a new fitness hub called #TikTokFitness, powered by Peloton. This collaboration aims to bring short-form fitness videos, live classes, instructor series, and celebrity collaborations to TikTok's vast audience. Following the announcement, Peloton's stock shares rose by 7%, signaling a positive market reaction to their efforts to recover from recent financial downturns, including another recent partnership with YouTube TV.

headline: FNGU ETF Analysis: Dividends, Returns AMEX:FNGU
content: This article provides an analysis of the MicroSectors FANG+ 3X Leveraged ETNs (FNGU), detailing its key statistics such as Assets Under Management ($1.47 billion), expense ratio (2.60%), and the fact that it does not pay dividends. It highlights FNGU's structure as a geared product with daily resets, making it suitable for short-term trading rather than long-term investment due to compounding effects. The ETF offers 3x exposure to an index of FANG companies and other similar businesses, with constituents being equally weighted.

headline: Aeva to supply sensors to Daimler Truck in $1 billion deal
content: Aeva Technologies has secured a $1 billion deal to supply lidar sensors to Daimler Truck for self-driving trucks, which are anticipated to be on U.S. roads by 2027. Aeva's sensors are designed to detect the speed of distant objects, aiding in collision avoidance. The agreement underscores continued interest in robotic trucking for long-haul routes despite challenges faced by self-driving passenger vehicle technology.

headline: Best Socially Responsible Investment Apps of January 2024
content: This article highlights the best socially responsible investment (SRI) apps for January 2024, detailing their features, pros, and cons. It explains what SRI is, differentiates it from ESG investing, and provides expert insights on the advantages and disadvantages of using these apps. The article reviews top platforms like IMPACT, Betterment, Sustainfolio, and Ellevest, among others, to help investors align their financial goals with their ethical values.

headline: FTI Consulting adds trio to Strategic Communications team
content: FTI Consulting has expanded its Strategic Communications practice in India by hiring Salonie Chawla as a Director, Snehil Singh as a Senior Consultant, and Shruti Vakhariya as a Consultant. These new additions bring diverse experience from government engagement, public policy, and financial communications to strengthen the team's capabilities in handling complex policy challenges and industry-side advisory for clients. The firm anticipates increased demand for such expertise given the disruptive business landscape expected in the coming 24 months.

headline: Bracken Darrell reimagined some of the world's biggest brands. Now he has plans to do it again
content: Bracken Darrell, the interim CEO of Vans and former CEO of Logitech, is known for his ability to reinvent brands through design. Now six months into his role at VF Corp (owner of brands like Vans, North Face, and Supreme), he aims to apply his turnaround expertise to the company. Darrell previously revitalized Logitech's product line and culture, emphasizing the importance of design in corporate success.

headline: Iridium Is Offering Its Own Smartphone-to-Satellite Service to Companies
content: Iridium has launched its own smartphone-to-satellite service, "Project Stardust," after its partnership with Qualcomm ended. This new service will allow original equipment manufacturers and carriers to offer text messaging and emergency SOS capabilities through Iridium's global low Earth orbit satellite constellation, adhering to 3GPP 5G standards. Initially focusing on data messaging, Iridium plans to begin testing in 2025 with service expected to start in 2026.

headline: SKYX’s All-in-One Smart Platform is Everything from a Smart Speaker to a Smoke Detector
content: SKYX Platforms Corp. debuted its patented All-in-One Smart Platform at CES 2024, aiming to make existing homes technologically advanced. This platform integrates multiple smart home features like a smoke/CO detector, smart speaker, Wi-Fi repeater, and various lighting controls, all controllable via app and voice commands. The product installs easily into a ceiling and supports major smart home ecosystems, with SKYX also renewing a global licensing agreement with GE.

headline: Software Glitch Behind Recalled App Could Drastically Increase Insulin Delivery
content: A software glitch in a recalled app has the potential to drastically increase insulin delivery, posing a significant health risk. This issue was highlighted on January 10, 2024, by Brian Bossetta.

headline: REX Shares and Tuttle Capital Management Expand T-REX Single-Stock ETF Suite with Apple, Alphabet, and Microsoft Offerings
content: REX Shares and Tuttle Capital Management have expanded their T-REX Single-Stock ETF suite by introducing new offerings for Apple (CBOE: AAPX), Alphabet (CBOE: GOOX), and Microsoft (CBOE: MSFX). These ETFs provide seasoned traders with 200% daily targeted exposure to these major tech companies. The expansion aims to offer advanced tools for precise positioning in the tech giants, building on the success of earlier NVIDIA and Tesla single-stock ETFs which have attracted over $100 million in assets since their October 2023 launch.

headline: Upcoming Events
content: REX Shares, in collaboration with Tuttle Capital Management, has expanded its T-REX Single-Stock ETF suite with new offerings providing 200% daily targeted exposure to Apple, Alphabet, and Microsoft. These ETFs (AAPX, GOOX, MSFX) are designed for seasoned traders to give leveraged exposure to major tech stocks. The T-REX suite, which debuted in October 2023, now covers diverse tech sectors and has already attracted over $100 million in assets.

headline: Taiwan's strength in semiconductors could be its 'Achilles heel,' economist says
content: An economist warns that Taiwan's heavy reliance on semiconductor exports, particularly to China, could become its "Achilles heel." Paul Cavey of East Asia Econ advises Taiwan to diversify its economy, as China's growing capacity for chip production could significantly impact Taiwan's economic future. This vulnerability is further exacerbated by the ongoing U.S.-China chip war and efforts by Western countries to restrict China's access to advanced chip technology.

headline: Optimizing Communication and Data Sharing in Multi-Core SoC Designs
content: This article discusses the evolution of interconnects in Systems-on-Chip (SoCs), from shared buses to Network-on-Chip (NoC) architectures, highlighting their role in managing data flow and enhancing performance. It delves into the importance of cache coherence for data consistency in multi-core designs and the challenges engineers face in optimizing communication and data sharing as semiconductor technology advances. The article also mentions Arteris' Ncore Cache Coherent Interconnect as a solution.

headline: Disney+ On Apple Vision Pro Ushers In A New Era Of Storytelling Innovation And Immersive Entertainment
content: Beginning February 2, Disney+ will be available on Apple Vision Pro, offering subscribers a new immersive streaming experience. Users can transform their spaces into iconic Disney environments and watch dozens of popular movies in 3D, leveraging advanced technology developed through the collaboration of Disney and Apple teams. This collaboration aims to bring fans closer to beloved stories and characters through groundbreaking technology.

headline: IDC: Apple sold more smartphones than Samsung for the first time in 2023
content: Apple Inc. surpassed Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. to become the world's largest smartphone manufacturer by unit shipments in 2023, according to a preliminary report by IDC. This marks the first time since 2010 that Samsung did not hold the top position. Despite an overall decline in global smartphone shipments for the year, Apple saw an increase in iPhone sales, particularly strong in the fourth quarter, whereas Samsung experienced a decline.

headline: Jabil announces collaboration with Fintech Leader Revolut
content: Jabil Inc. announced its ongoing collaboration with Revolut, a digital banking pioneer, to support the neobank's growth and global expansion in merchant acquiring. Jabil provides custom, pre-certified Point-of-Sale (POS) hardware platforms, including the Revolut Reader, which enables merchants to accept various in-store and on-the-go payments. The partnership highlights Jabil's role in accelerating market entry and providing comprehensive product design, development, and manufacturing solutions for Revolut's innovative payment solutions.

headline: Microsoft Monetizing Copilot, Round 2; Synopsys Pays Big for Ansys
content: Microsoft is expanding the monetization of its AI-powered Copilot by removing the minimum seat requirement for Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions, allowing single users to purchase it. Simultaneously, Synopsys has agreed to acquire Ansys in a significant $35 billion cash and stock deal, marking a major merger in the chip design and engineering simulation software industries for 2024.

headline: Supreme Court rejects Apple's appeal on App Store fees amid Epic Games legal battle
content: The Supreme Court has rejected Apple's appeal regarding its App Store fees, allowing a lower court order to take effect. This decision could force Apple to permit app developers to offer alternative payment options, potentially reducing Apple's commission revenue. The ruling stems from an antitrust lawsuit filed by Epic Games, although Epic's broader antitrust claims against Apple were also rejected.

headline: Unlocking The Potential Of Pure Research At InterDigital
content: This article examines InterDigital's role as a pure research facility, led by CEO Liren Chen, and its significant contributions to wireless technology, including current work on 5G advanced and future plans for 6G with AI integration. It highlights InterDigital's impressive growth, long-standing partnerships with companies like Apple and Amazon, and its unique approach to fostering innovation among its largely inventor-based workforce. Chen emphasizes the importance of curiosity, competency, and impact in driving both individual and company success, showcasing InterDigital's continued influence on global digital communication.

headline: 5 key themes from the 2024 Consumer Electronics Show
content: The 2024 Consumer Electronics Show (CES) highlighted five key technological themes: AI as a pervasive enabler across all tech, advancements in smart home devices with unified communication standards like Matter, the evolution of immersive technology anticipating the Apple Vision Pro, the future of the automotive industry focusing on driver experience and electric vehicles, and the widening scope of health technology, including AI-powered mental wellness tools and wearables. These innovations provide a glimpse into the technological future.

headline: Apple Inc. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
content: Apple Inc.'s stock experienced a 0.52% decline, closing at $182.68 on Wednesday, marking its second consecutive day of losses. This occurred during an overall negative trading session where the NASDAQ Composite fell by 0.59% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average decreased by 0.25%. Despite the daily loss, the article title suggests Apple's stock performance still outpaced the broader market.

headline: What Does 2024 Hold for the Magnificent Seven?
content: The "Magnificent Seven" stocks, including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla, drove 73% of stock market gains in 2023 due to superior earnings growth and profit margins. While some analysts predict a pullback in 2024 due to potential overvaluation and cyclicality, others believe their strong forecasted earnings growth could lead to continued outperformance, especially while interest rates remain elevated. The article highlights contrasting fortunes early in 2024, with Nvidia surging and Tesla facing its worst January since its IPO.

headline: Your S&P 500 Index Fund Has Higher Risk Than You May Think
content: This article argues that the S&P 500 index fund, traditionally seen as diversified, now carries higher risk due to its concentration in a few technology stocks. It highlights concentration, valuation, and inflation risks, suggesting investors re-evaluate their S&P 500 holdings and consider more value-oriented, truly diversified investments.

headline: More Computer Magazine Lore: A 1983 Nastygram from Wayne Green
content: This article provides additional lore surrounding computer magazines, focusing on Wayne Green, a colorful and controversial figure in tech publishing. It details his eccentric career, his contentious relationship with figures like Steve Jobs and David Bunnell, and his impact on early computer magazines like Byte, PC World, and Macworld. The post highlights a "nastygram" Green sent in response to PC World's premiere issue, shedding light on the competitive landscape of the 1980s computer magazine industry.

headline: Higher S&P 500 Earnings Could Benefit This Active ETF
content: The NEOS S&P 500 High Income ETF (SPYI) is poised to benefit from expected higher corporate earnings in 2024, as forecasted by Goldman Sachs. SPYI, an actively managed ETF, focuses on call options and holds "Magnificent Seven" stocks, offering investors tailor-made holdings, risk mitigation, and tax-efficient monthly income. Its active management removes the need for constant supervision and provides a single solution for a core equity portfolio.

headline: Corning's Indian JV signs $120 mln investment deal with Tamil Nadu state
content: Corning's Indian joint venture, Bharat Innovative Glass Technologies, has signed an agreement with the Tamil Nadu state to invest 10 billion rupees ($120.4 million) to establish a new facility. This plant will manufacture front cover glass for mobile phones and phone parts, highlighting India's growing importance as a manufacturing hub amid a global shift in supply chains away from China. The investment is part of larger efforts by the Indian government to promote local manufacturing and has attracted other major electronics manufacturers and Apple suppliers.

headline: The Best Desktop PCs: Early 2024
content: This article provides a comprehensive guide to the best pre-built desktop PCs available in early 2024, categorizing them for different needs such as gaming, all-in-one solutions, and mini PCs. It offers detailed recommendations including specific models like the Corsair Vengeance for gaming, HP Envy 34 AIO for creative work, and Apple Mac Mini M2 for compactness. The guide also discusses considerations between building a PC and buying pre-built, and factors like value, upgradeability, and space constraints.

headline: ‘Find My®’ Alternative Guide
content: The article provides a guide to alternatives to Apple's "Find My" app. It highlights Life360 as a location sharing and family safety application.

headline: 10 Best Project Management Software for Windows
content: This article reviews the 10 best project management software solutions compatible with Windows, comparing their features, pricing, and specific strengths suitable for different team needs. It highlights tools like monday.com for customized workflows, Smartsheet for collaboration, Microsoft Project for scheduling, and Jira for software development, providing guidance on how to choose the right software based on budget, team size, and essential features. The article also addresses common FAQs regarding Windows project management tools, including Microsoft Project's capabilities and its transition to the upgraded Microsoft Planner.

headline: Apple device management software company Jamf plans to layoff 6% of employees
content: Jamf, an Apple device management software company, announced a workforce reduction plan to lay off approximately 6% of its full-time employees. This move is intended to reduce operating costs, improve operating margins, and achieve profitable growth. The company expects to incur between $6.6 and $8.2 million in charges for severance and related expenses, primarily in the first quarter of 2024.

headline: Behind Target’s ‘Winning Retail Formula’
content: Target Corp. actively expanded and renovated its stores in 2023, opening 21 new locations and remodeling over 160. The company's strategy focuses on a superior shopping experience through large-format stores, expanded assortments, enhanced fulfillment services, and strategic partnerships. Target plans further investments and new locations in 2024, continuing its growth trajectory in the retail sector.

headline: Companies are struggling to keep private data safe from generative AI, Cisco says
content: A new Cisco report indicates that despite corporate bans and restrictions on generative AI tools, employees are still entering private company data into them. The survey of 2,600 privacy and security professionals found that a significant number of companies have either banned or limited AI usage due to concerns about data leaks and intellectual property infringement. This highlights a struggle for companies to balance the benefits of AI with the imperative to protect sensitive information.

headline: Newegg Debuts Newegg Refreshed Program to Offer Quality Resale Products at Low Prices
content: Newegg has launched "Newegg Refreshed," a new program offering refurbished tech products at competitive prices, including Apple goods, graphics cards, and gaming PCs. The program also integrates Newegg's graphics card trade-in service and provides a 90-day return guarantee. Newegg emphasizes both cost savings for customers and environmental benefits through product reuse.

headline: AI & The Dragon: What Trends Will Dominate 2024?
content: In 2024, Emerging Markets (EM) are expected to rebound, driven by potential Fed rate cuts and a weakening US dollar, with China and Brazil presenting more attractive valuations than the "Magnificent Seven" and other EM ex-China countries. The article suggests focusing on long-term trends and strategic allocations to specific growth sectors within EM. China's "Year of the Dragon" is anticipated to bring a gradual recovery in consumer sentiment and real estate, supported by government policies and significant expected EPS growth.

headline: Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) Seeks FDA Nod for Next-Gen da Vinci 5
content: Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) has applied for FDA 510(k) clearance for its next-generation da Vinci 5 multiport surgical robot and expects approval and launch later this year. The company is actively preparing manufacturing facilities for the new system while also engaging regulators in Japan and South Korea for approval. This development comes as the company's shares lost value a year ago due to the absence of a new multiport system announcement.

headline: Popular Inc. reports $541M in net income in 2023, $94.6M in 4Q
content: Popular Inc. reported a net income of $541.3 million for 2023, down from $1.1 billion in 2022, with $94.6 million in the fourth quarter. These figures include a $71.4 million expense due to a special FDIC assessment. Excluding this assessment, adjusted net income for 2023 was $586.6 million, and CEO Ignacio Álvarez noted stable net interest income, loan growth, and strong client activity despite market disruptions.

headline: What Gentex’s Acquisition Of eSight Means For The Electronic Eyewear Market
content: Gentex Corporation has acquired Toronto-based eSight, a move that could significantly impact the electronic eyewear market for the visually impaired. This acquisition follows a partnership that led to the eSight Go, a new electronic eyewear system that is more affordable, lighter, and offers improved performance compared to its predecessor. Gentex's expertise in electro-optical products and manufacturing capabilities is expected to drive down costs and enhance the technology for sight enhancement wearables.

headline: Apple Inc. stock underperforms Monday when compared to competitors
content: Apple Inc. (AAPL) stock underperformed on Monday, closing down 0.36% at $191.73, despite a generally positive trading session for the broader market. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for Apple, contrasting with gains seen in the NASDAQ Composite Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

headline: XLK ETF: A Better Way To Invest In Microsoft But Volatility Comes First (NYSEARCA:XLK)
content: The Technology Select Sector ETF (XLK) has appreciated over 20% since October 2023, now trading above $200. The author maintains a positive outlook, attributing potential growth to top holdings like Microsoft and other software companies benefiting from AI's move into exploitation. Despite volatility risks from Fed policies and Apple's earnings, XLK is considered undervalued compared to Microsoft and Nvidia, with a target price around $223.

headline: 2027 the Target for Transition Away from 1D GTIN, Toward Digital Link 2D Barcodes
content: The packaging industry is targeting 2027 for a significant transition from the traditional 1D GTIN barcode to the more versatile Digital Link 2D barcode. This shift, driven by increasing consumer demand for information, regulatory requirements, and supply chain traceability needs, will enable a single QR code to provide different information to various stakeholders (consumers, retailers, supply chain partners). The "Sunrise 2027" program aims to prepare the necessary infrastructure, primarily software changes, for this industry-wide adoption.

headline: Apple Inc. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
content: Apple Inc. (AAPL) shares fell 1.92% to $188.04 on Tuesday, marking its fifth consecutive day of losses. This underperformance occurred on a mixed trading day, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising and the NASDAQ Composite Index falling. The article highlights Apple's stock decline relative to its competitors and broader market movements.

headline: Corning beats quarterly sales estimates, signals improving demand for fiber optics
content: Corning exceeded Wall Street's fourth-quarter adjusted sales estimates, driven by increasing demand for optical fiber cables used in data centers for generative AI applications. Despite a slight dip in optical communications segment sales, the company observes "green shoots" in the hyperscale data center space. Although Q4 earnings met expectations, Corning provided a conservative profit outlook for the current quarter, expecting it to be the low point of the year.

headline: Gogoro Unveils New Flagship Smartscooter, Pulse
content: Gogoro Inc. (Nasdaq: GGR) has unveiled its new flagship Smartscooter, the Pulse, which features an aerodynamic design and a hyperdrive powertrain enabling it to reach 0-50km/h in 3.05 seconds. The Pulse integrates advanced features such as an active-matrix lighting system, a 10.25-inch panoramic HD touch display powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon QWM2290 digital chassis, and Apple Wallet and Apple Find My integration. The Smartscooter is expected to begin shipping in Taiwan in late Q2 2024, aiming to set a new standard for high-performance electric two-wheelers.

headline: Payments firm PayPal to reduce global workforce by 9% in 2024
content: Payments firm PayPal Holdings is set to cut approximately 2,500 jobs, or 9% of its global workforce, in 2024 through layoffs and the elimination of open roles. This decision, announced by CEO Alex Chriss, aims to "right-size" the company for efficiency and profitable growth amidst competitive pressures and a need to improve margins. The move follows similar cost-cutting measures by competitor Block.

headline: Tile vs. AirTag™: Which Bluetooth Tracker Should You Choose?
content: This article asks the question of whether a Tile or an AirTag is the better Bluetooth tracker. However, the provided content is incomplete, only listing the title and a company name, so no further details can be extracted.

headline: Alcoa to supply Nexans with low-carbon aluminum, including metal from ELYSIS™ technology
content: Alcoa will supply Nexans with low-carbon aluminum rod, including metal produced using the breakthrough ELYSIS™ technology, which eliminates direct greenhouse gas emissions from the traditional smelting process. Nexans will be the first cable manufacturer globally to utilize metal from this process in various cable types. This collaboration further strengthens the long-standing relationship between the two companies, with Alcoa already supplying Nexans with EcoLum™ low-carbon aluminum.

headline: Apple Inc. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
content: Apple Inc. (AAPL) shares rose 1.33% to $186.86 on Thursday, breaking a six-day losing streak. Despite this gain, the stock underperformed compared to the broader market, as the NASDAQ Composite Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average both saw larger percentage increases on the same day.

headline: Aptiv to cut stake in Motional, self-driving JV with Hyundai
content: Aptiv, a US autonomous driving technology company, has decided to significantly reduce its stake in Motional, a self-driving joint venture with Hyundai Motor Group, and will cease injecting additional capital. Motional, which has accumulated 1 trillion won ($750 million) in deficits, had requested further funding from both partners. This decision puts pressure on Hyundai Motor Group to decide on its own additional capital injection, highlighting the ongoing financial and commercial challenges in the autonomous vehicle industry.

headline: Box Brings Your Content to Life with the Box App for Apple Vision Pro
content: Box Inc. has launched a new app for Apple Vision Pro, leveraging spatial computing to transform how users interact with content in the enterprise. The Box app for Apple Vision Pro offers immersive experiences for various industries, including construction, retail, manufacturing, and education. It provides secure collaboration and productivity features, integrating with Box's Content Cloud, and will be available for free on the App Store for visionOS on February 2, 2024.

headline: Apple, Skechers fall; Amazon, Deckers Outdoor rise, Friday, 2/2/2024
content: On Friday, February 2, 2024, several major stocks experienced significant price changes. Apple and Skechers saw declines due to lukewarm forecasts, while Amazon, Deckers Outdoor, Meta Platforms, and Clorox rose following strong financial results or optimistic outlooks. Microchip Technology and Columbia Sportswear also faced drops after giving disappointing forecasts.

headline: Disney Heads into the Future on the Apple Vision Pro
content: The Walt Disney Company is launching Disney+ on Apple's Vision Pro, marking a new chapter in immersive storytelling. This integration allows viewers to experience Disney+ content in virtual environments like Star Wars' Tatooine or Marvel's Avengers Tower, and watch 3D versions of popular films. The partnership highlights Disney's long-standing focus on blending technology with creativity to enhance entertainment experiences.

headline: Markets Brief: Will the ‘Magnificent Seven’ Stocks Keep Carrying the Market After Earnings?
content: The article analyzes the performance of the "Magnificent Seven" stocks after their latest earnings reports, noting that while most beat forecasts, market reactions were mixed due to high expectations. It discusses whether these tech giants can continue to drive market gains in 2024, given their current valuations and the potential for a broader market rally. The article also provides a detailed recap of individual company performances and analyst commentary.

headline: Vishay Unveils New High-Speed Photodiode for Wearable Devices
